clue.text: Escape from epidemic?

definitions.meaning: a getaway, as from a prison
a sudden spread of a disease, an outbreak

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a region gripped by a plague.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a prison getaway and, with the question mark admitting it is a stretch, a sudden eruption of disease.

clue.text: Band "B" accommodation

parts.note: read 'Band "B"' as the letters B and B, the usual short name for a guesthouse offering a room and a morning meal

explanation.surface: Lodging graded in the second price tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Guesthouse lodging that includes a morning meal is known by the initials B&B.

clue.text: German eleven at home show little character

parts.note: the German word for eleven is elf
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A German football team playing at home puts on a weak display of personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' is a link word. The surface suggests a team (an eleven) lacking character; the definition is a noun, an old word for a small elf or child.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is an old term for a small sprite or urchin, a tiny figure.

clue.text: Timber fault — sounds incomplete

indicators.note: the clue says the word for incomplete is what we hear, not what is written

parts.note: something incomplete is not whole

explanation.surface: A defect in wood is described as sounding unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not whole' said aloud gives the hole left in a plank where a knot has fallen out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a plank where a knot has dropped out is a flaw in the wood.

clue.text: Unlit interchange, up to a point

indicators.note: to interchange is to swap things around, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark road junction, as far as it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a preposition meaning as far as a certain time or point and no further.

clue.text: Odds called for suddenly leapt up

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds on a horse when a race begins
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Betting prices were demanded, and someone jumped to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word. SP (starting price) is the racecourse term for the final odds offered on a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means jumped quickly upward, a past tense of spring.

clue.text: Express admiration for lift, after parking

indicators.note: after places the word for lift behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to lift is to raise

explanation.surface: Someone compliments a ride offered once the car is parked.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or commend someone is to speak well of them.

clue.text: Ideal song may be rendered close by

indicators.note: to render is to perform or convert, so the letters of the two words before are recast

explanation.surface: A perfect tune might be performed nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means next to or beside, so near at hand.

clue.text: Re-collate engine redesigned to allow representative selection

indicators.note: something redesigned is put together in a new form, so the letters of the two words before are reordered

explanation.surface: Sort the papers again and rebuild the motor so that a fair choice can be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To allow' is link wording. The anagram uses all fifteen letters of RECOLLATE and ENGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A national vote choosing members of a parliament selects the people's representatives.

clue.text: Burglaries — sin?

parts.note: the instruction to break up the letters INS produces the word sin, so the answer is the wordplay that would build the clue word

explanation.surface: Asks whether house thefts are wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, break INS, and the result is SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal entries into houses or premises in order to steal are thefts of that kind.

clue.text: Ice-breaker rested for refit

indicators.note: a refit means rebuilding, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship that cuts through ice is laid up to be overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice-breaker' suggests a ship, but it is a device in a fridge or car that clears ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that melts frost from a freezer or windscreen breaks the ice up.

clue.text: A party sailors held on deck

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors of Britain

explanation.surface: Navy crews hold a party up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held on' is link wording. 'Deck' looks like part of a ship but is the verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate or embellish it.

clue.text: On course to play the second half after this

definitions.text: On course to play the second half after this

parts.words: On course to play the second half after this
parts.note: on a golf course, the back nine holes are played once the hole that ends the front nine is done

explanation.surface: A golfer on track to finish the round after this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On course' means on the golf course; a standard round is eighteen holes, split into two halves of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hole numbered after eight ends the front half of an eighteen-hole golf round.

clue.text: New foals on a rug, playing — sweet!

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of the word after are rearranged
playing about with letters shuffles them, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Young horses frolicking on a rug look adorable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word. 'New' turns FOALS into LOAF and 'playing' turns A RUG into SUGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined sugar moulded into a conical block is a sweetener.

clue.text: Naval vessel manoeuvring past the bill — left abandoned

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters of the remaining words are rearranged
something abandoned is left behind, so one letter is dropped from the phrase

explanation.surface: A warship steams past the headland of Portland Bill, with the coast left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' drops one L from PAST THE BILL, leaving PASTTHEBIL, and 'manoeuvring' rearranges those ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavily armed warship is a naval vessel.

clue.text: Battle column

definitions.meaning: a naval engagement of 1805 in which Nelson defeated the French and Spanish fleets
Nelson's Column in London's ... Square, built to commemorate that victory

explanation.surface: A monument to a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column stands in Trafalgar Square in central London, commemorating the 1805 sea battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to Nelson's great 1805 sea victory and to the London square whose column honours it.

clue.text: Mark urban shortage

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
urban means relating to a city

explanation.surface: A town lacks a feature that would mark it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or insufficiency of something is a dearth.

clue.text: Dig up cash container

definitions.meaning: to turn over soil for planting
the drawer of money in a shop

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to cultivate land by turning the soil and also a shop's money drawer or register.

clue.text: Pool cover?

parts.note: not a sheet stretched over a swimming pool but what bathers wear to cover themselves in it

explanation.definitionFit: Costumes and trunks are what people wear to cover themselves at the baths.

clue.text: Afternoon paper?

parts.note: after noon it is no longer morning, so it is ...-........, and a test paper sat then fits the bill

explanation.definitionFit: A test sat by students is called a paper, and split as 'ex a.m.' it means past morning.

clue.text: Wisely head off to get printing disc

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is wise to set off to fetch a part for the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a beheading of 'Wisely' or 'set out', but 'off' alone is the anagram signal and 'head' is fodder; 'to get' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: An old typewriter and printer part was a rotating wheel of spokes, each tipped with a character.

clue.text: Also a blow-up

parts.note: to swell is to blow up or inflate, used here as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means too or in addition.

clue.text: Sound sleep gets rid of bags

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that is heard like the word for sleep rather than spelt like it

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
to sack someone is to get rid of them

explanation.surface: A good deep sleep gets rid of the bags under someone's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound sleep' looks like deep sleep, but 'Sound' signals that NAP is heard, spelt KNAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rucksacks carried on the back are bags for hikers.

clue.text: Ocean sounds appropriate

indicators.note: sounds tells the solver that the word for ocean is heard rather than written

parts.note: the oceans are the seas

explanation.surface: The sea makes a fitting noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning fitting but is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take possession of it, to grab it.

clue.text: Crazy cinema production cutting last scene

indicators.note: a production makes something new, so the letters of cinema are rearranged
cutting removes something, so a letter is taken out of the word cinema
the last letter of scene is its final E

explanation.surface: A frantic film shoot ends with the final scene being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting last scene' removes E (the last letter of 'scene') from CINEMA, leaving CINMA, which 'production' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied, wildly excited behaviour is described as mad.

clue.text: No old horse's cry

parts.note: the old word for no is nay, and a horse saying it would make the familiar whinnying call

explanation.definitionFit: The high whinnying call of a horse sounds like the old refusal 'nay'.

clue.text: Old English settler's point of view

definitions.meaning: one of the Germanic people who settled in England in the 5th century
a perspective or slant on a subject

explanation.surface: An early settler's outlook on life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic tribe who gave England its name, and a slant or perspective is also this word.

clue.text: Heard to try twins' nerves

indicators.note: heard means the word for try is what we hear, written differently

parts.note: taken as written and then spoken
Gemini is the Twins in the zodiac

explanation.surface: Bringing up twins tests a parent's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is a link word. Gemini, the sign of the Twins, gives the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth cranial nerves, which serve the face, are called trigeminal nerves; this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Kick-start the human race into longer life

indicators.note: the start of each of the following words gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Give humanity a boost towards living longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick-start' looks like one word, but 'Kick' is the definition and 'start' takes the first letters of the next six words.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick in the informal sense is a buzz of excitement.

clue.text: Deteriorate badly in the war

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the words after are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Things go seriously downhill during wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming worn or feeble over time is a way of declining.
